detail.abstract: The digital discovery landscape is undergoing structural transformation. Zero-click searches—queries resolved without navigation to external websites—now represent 58.5% of all search activity in the United States and European Union [SparkToro/Datos, 2024]. Concurrently, AI-powered answer engines are emerging as primary information interfaces, with platforms such as ChatGPT reaching 400 million weekly active users [OpenAI, 2024]. This convergence is fundamentally altering how consumers and enterprises discover, evaluate, and select products and services. This paper analyzes the market dynamics driving the zero-click paradigm, examines projected impacts across industry sectors, and introduces a framework for understanding organizational readiness. Research indicates that organizations optimizing for AI citation achieve 40% or greater visibility improvements in generative search results [Princeton/Georgia Tech, 2024]. However, the majority of enterprises remain unprepared for this transition, with Gartner projecting a 50% decline in traditional organic traffic by 2028 [Gartner, 2024]. The findings suggest that competitive advantage in the emerging landscape will accrue to organizations that establish authority within AI knowledge systems, implement structured data architectures for machine comprehension, and develop measurement frameworks capable of attributing value to non-click interaction.

detail.abstract: The swift progression of digital marketing in India is fuelled by technological advancements, shifting consumer behaviours, and the growing prevalence of the internet and mobile devices. Within the Indian context, this document, entitled "Emerging Trends in Digital Marketing: A Glimpse into the Future in India," delves into the pivotal trends influencing the future of digital marketing. Noteworthy trends encompass artificial intelligence, machine learning, voice search, and video marketing. influencer collaborations and localized content are examined for their impact on marketing strategies. The study also delves into the challenges and ethical considerations accompanying these developments, such as data privacy and security concerns. Through case studies of successful campaigns, this paper highlights the opportunities and potential growth areas for businesses to leverage these trends effectively. The findings underscore the need for marketers to stay agile and adaptive to maintain a competitive edge in the dynamic landscape of digital marketing in India.

title: Predicting OTT Subscription Behavior using Deep Learning: A Multi-Class Classification Approach with Feature Engineering and Class Imbalance Handling

detail.title: Predicting OTT Subscription Behavior using Deep Learning: A Multi-Class Classification Approach with Feature Engineering and Class Imbalance Handling
detail.abstract: With the introduction of different OTT streaming platforms like Netflix, Amazon Prime Video, and Disney+ Hotstar, subscription user behavior has become important factors in building customer retention, pricing, and content recommendations. These methodologies do not address the nonlinear relationships that exist between important variables like pricing, quality of content, discount availability, and payment options. This study forms the basis for developing a deep learning approach to predicting subscription behavior for OTT platforms based on a multi-layer perceptron (MLP) model. Preprocessing of the survey data for feature selection, label encoding, and normalization will include addressing the class imbalance on the dataset using SMOTE for balanced learning. The architecture contains batch normalization and dropout regularization, with training carried out using Adam optimizer for 500 epochs. Model application achieved a very high accuracy of 97%, which is further validated on various classification metrics as well as confusion and accuracy-loss plots. The study pinpoints pricing, promotions, and satisfaction with content as the prominent factors responsible for subscription choices.

title: A Hybrid Deep Learning and XGBoost Framework for Predicting OTT Subscription Timing Based on user Behavior Analysis
affiliations: and Parul University

detail.title: A Hybrid Deep Learning and XGBoost Framework for Predicting OTT Subscription Timing Based on user Behavior Analysis
detail.abstract: The rapid expansion of Over-the-Top (OTT) streaming services has resulted in growing competitive pressures on platforms to better understand their subscribers and retain them. In this study, we outline a hybrid predictive framework; a deep-learning based feature extractor integrated with an XGBoost classifier for predicting the timing of users' last OTT subscription. The data is collected through an online structured survey that contained questions on viewing habits, preferred platforms, and influential factors. To manage class imbalance to improve the models performance, we applied the Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE) to the training data. We trained a deep neural network with focal loss to produce meaningful intermediate feature representations for training a multi-class XGBoost classifier. The proposed model produced a test accuracy of approximately 93%. In-depth visualizations of the generated model including class distribution, confusion matrix, and recall at the class distribution level allowed us to evaluate and understand the model performance. This combined predictive framework is able to enhance classification accuracy and now characterizes user behavioral trends. The framework is applicable in areas such as individualized marketing, assessing churn, and analyzing subscription cycle; which is of great use for OTT service providers seeking to best utilize user engagement initiatives.

title: Robust Pricing in Marketing Channels
affiliations: University of California, Davis - Graduate School of Management

detail.title: Robust Pricing in Marketing Channels
detail.abstract: In many cases, managers cannot rely on expected profit maximization to determine prices due to a lack of reliable sales data. To overcome this issue, the pricing literature suggests adopting strategies that are robust to model uncertainty. However, most of this literature addresses situations where firms sell directly to consumers, leaving a gap in understanding how to implement robust pricing strategies when products are sold through retailers. To address this gap, we propose a model that explores the impact of robustness on pricing strategies for both manufacturers and retailers. The model provides three novel insights. First, we find that in equilibrium, channel partners will seek different levels of robustness for their pricing decisions. Second, the model reveals that injecting robustness in channel pricing decisions can not only help manage unforeseeable demand shocks, as it should be, but also mitigate double marginalization. Finally, the model uncovers that a decentralized channel can generate more profit than the centralized channel when robust pricing strategies are implemented.

detail.abstract: This conceptual paper introduces branded embodiments: body movements that symbolise brands, and explores how consumers co-create them to contest consumption. We identify how both pro- and anti-brand consumers co-create them to reject and promote consumption; however, whereas pro-brand consumers support the brand and oppose rivals, anti-brand consumers reject the brand and support rivals. Identity compels these polarised meanings as consumers seek to affirm (dis)identification and boundaries with outsiders. Branded embodiments support identity mechanisms as the body is efficient for social identity construction and experiences in interaction rituals. We offer insights into body movements within branding, anti-consumption, consumer-brand co-creation, and rivalry.

detail.title: Social Media Insights from the Middle East in 2023
detail.abstract:
This report examines social media trends and developments across the Middle East and North Africa (MENA) region during 2023, the twelfth annual study in a series that began in 2012. Drawing on analysis of over 100 sources, including industry reports, academic studies, news media coverage, platform announcements, and social media posts, the research documents how social media platforms, practices, and policies evolved across one of the world's most dynamic digital landscapes during a particularly consequential year. 

The study reveals three overarching themes that characterized 2023: accelerated platform innovation and regional partnerships, with Meta, Snapchat, YouTube, and TikTok launching new services and creator tools tailored to MENA markets; intensified concerns about social media's impact on youth wellbeing and addiction, highlighted by the Arab Youth Survey 2023 finding that nearly three-quarters of young people struggle to disconnect from social media; and heightened scrutiny of social media's role in spreading misinformation and facilitating government surveillance, particularly following the October 2023 outbreak of the Israel-Hamas war. 

The study provides a detailed analysis of major platforms, including Facebook, Instagram, WhatsApp, Telegram, Snapchat, YouTube, TikTok, and X (formerly Twitter), examining user demographics, market penetration, platform innovations, and commercial developments. Key findings include: the UAE ranking first globally for average number of social media platforms used monthly (8.3); seven of the ten biggest global markets for TikTok (by population percentage) being in the Middle East; and social media advertising in the region reaching $3.4 billion in 2023, representing over half of total digital ad spending. 

The findings have significant implications for understanding digital communication in complex geopolitical environments, platform governance in authoritarian contexts, and the intersection of commercial technology platforms with freedom of expression, misinformation, and state surveillance. The research documents a region where social media simultaneously serves as a space for creative expression, commercial opportunity, political organizing, and social connection, even as platforms face mounting pressures to address content harms, protect user privacy, and navigate competing demands across dramatically different political and cultural contexts.

detail.abstract: The current research examines the impact of using AI-generated images (vs. real photographs) in social media posts of green influencers, by relying on schema congruity theory. Three experimental studies show that compared to posts using real photographs, posts that use AI-generated images are less likely to receive favorable consumer responses. This effect arises from incongruity between gen-AI and the green schema activated by the post, which causes a) lower perceived appropriateness of a gen-AI image to the green context, leading to b) lower perceived authenticity of the post. In attempting to counter this negative impact of the use of AI, a reason for the use of gen-AI is ineffective but images generated by purpose-built AI that aligns with the green cause fully mitigates the observed issue. By identifying and explaining the specific negative impact of gen-AI use on green influencers, this work extends research on gen-AI use by influencers in general and research on the negative impact of gen-AI in marketing. Findings of this research encourage green influencers and sustainable brands to use gen-AI cautiously.

detail.title: Do Accessibility Features Improve the Outdoor Mobility of People with Disabilities? An Empirical Study on Amap
detail.abstract: As of 2023, an estimated 1.3 billion people, or roughly 16% of the global population, have a disability. Big tech companies have played a significant role in improving disability inclusion by using technology to increase accessibility of their products/services. Although these approaches are promising, empirical evidence on their actual impact remains scarce. In this study, we examine how the accessibility feature in a location-based service app affects the outdoor mobility of disabled users. Using individual-level data from Amap, we find that this feature significantly increases disabled users’ exploration of outdoor spaces, whether through search or walk navigation. The effect holds for nearly all subgroups studied and either reduces or enlarges the gap among them. However, the positive effects are largely driven by a strong novelty-induced spike immediately after adoption, indicating limited long-term effect. Nevertheless, users exhibit persistent behavioral changes after adoption by searching for more distant locations but walking to closer destinations than before.

title: Are Inferred Order of Entry Effects on Firm Performance Economically Insightful?
affiliations: University of Illinois at Urbana-Champaign

detail.title: Are Inferred Order of Entry Effects on Firm Performance Economically Insightful?
detail.abstract: Order-of-entry effects are commonly studied by regressing firm performance on entry timing in reduced-form analyses. This paper shows that such regressions are inherently uninformative about whether observed order advantages reflect strategic deterrence motives. Using a theoretically grounded decomposition of entry incentives in dynamic oligopoly games, I show that reduced-form order-of-entry coefficients combine variation from direct profit motives, strategic deterrence, and cost heterogeneity. The resulting object generally differs from both the causal effect of entry timing and structural measures of deterrence. As a consequence, even precisely estimated order-of-entry effects, cannot be reliably interpreted as evidence for or against strategic deterrence. The analysis clarifies why order-of-entry patterns, while empirically robust, provide a poor diagnostic for the mechanisms governing firms’ entry decisions.

title: Staking Services: Taxonomy, Risks and Regulation

detail.title: Staking Services: Taxonomy, Risks and Regulation
detail.abstract:
This article provides a comprehensive legal and regulatory analysis of blockchain staking and staking services within proof-of-stake (PoS) networks, positioning staking as a foundational infrastructure of contemporary crypto-asset markets and decentralized finance (DeFi). Staking is examined as the process by which crypto-assets are locked to participate in transaction validation and network security, through an incentive and sanction mechanism based on rewards and slashing. The paper develops a functional taxonomy of staking models, distinguishing between solo staking, delegated (non-custodial) staking, and custodial staking, and further analyses ancillary services such as validator-as-a-service, pooling, early unbonding, slashing insurance, and liquid staking derivatives.

A structured risk taxonomy is proposed, separating risks affecting individual token holders (operational risk, counterparty risk, information asymmetry, custody and slashing exposure) from systemic risks for the blockchain ecosystem, including validator concentration, governance centralization, and potential threats to decentralization. From a legal perspective, the study assesses the regulatory treatment of staking under EU law, with particular reference to Regulation (EU) 2023/1114 on Markets in Crypto-assets (MiCAR), ESMA guidance, and comparative approaches adopted by the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission and the Swiss Financial Market Supervisory Authority (FINMA). The analysis shows that staking, in its pure technical form, is generally not classified as a regulated financial service or crypto-asset service, while custodial and pooled staking arrangements may trigger licensing, prudential, and investor-protection requirements.

The paper contributes to the scholarly literature on blockchain governance, crypto-asset regulation, and DeFi by offering a systematic framework for the legal qualification of staking, identifying open issues concerning contractual structures, consumer protection, and the regulatory perimeter of liquid staking and institutional participation. It is intended as a reference source for researchers in financial law, blockchain law, and regulatory studies seeking an in-depth overview of the taxonomy, risks, and legal treatment of staking in proof-of-stake blockchain networks.

title: Reduce and Reveal: Emissions Abatement and Disclosure in Supply Chains
affiliations: University of Kansas, School of Business

detail.title: Reduce and Reveal: Emissions Abatement and Disclosure in Supply Chains
detail.abstract:
Problem definition: We study the relationship between emissions abatement and emissions disclosure in a firm's supply chain. The firm first exerts effort to abate emissions and then discloses its emissions to investors to maximize its payoff. This payoff depends on its capital market valuation, determined by investors based on the reported emissions, and on an emissions cost incurred if the reported emissions are high. We first study a voluntary disclosure setting in which the firm strategically decides how informative its disclosure will be. We then compare this setting with mandatory disclosure under which the firm must report emissions accurately. 
Methodology/results: We develop an analytical model to characterize the firm's optimal information policy under voluntary disclosure and its abatement effort under both voluntary and mandatory disclosures. 
Managerial implications: We show that the firm's emissions reporting strategy under voluntary disclosure takes one of three forms. When the abatement cost is low, the firm sometimes reports low emissions as high, engaging in greenhushing. When the abatement cost is high, but the emissions cost is low, the firm sometimes reports high emissions as low, engaging in greenwashing. Finally, when both costs are high, the firm releases an uninformative, boilerplate disclosure that conveys no meaningful information. These commonly observed reporting strategies can thus emerge endogenously from economic incentives alone, without relying on behavioral explanations or political pressure, as prior work often posits. Moreover, intuition suggests that a greenwashing firm exerts little abatement effort, making mandatory disclosure beneficial, while a greenhushing firm already abates heavily, implying that a disclosure mandate would have limited impact. We show this need not be the case. When the firm greenhushes, a disclosure mandate increases abatement effort; however, when it greenwashes, mandatory disclosure reduces abatement effort and can harm both investors and the environment.

detail.abstract: The prevailing legal paradigm for cybersecurity liability is predicated on a 'catastrophic' model of harm, where liability attaches only upon the materialisation of a data breach. This 'breach-centric' orthodoxy fails to account for the invisible, latent, and systemic risks inherent in modern digital ecosystems risks that exist in the 'dwelling' phase of an attack long before exfiltration occurs. This article challenges the doctrinal insistence on 'concrete injury' in US jurisprudence (the Spokeo/TransUnion lineage) and contrasts it with the actuarial reality of the cyber-insurance market, which actively prices latent risks such as 'bricking,' 'dormant malware,' and 'resilience debt.' Drawing on Ulrich Beck's 'Risk Society' theory and an empirical analysis of 50 insurance coverage disputes, this research introduces a novel theoretical framework: 'Resilience Liability.' This framework argues that the maintenance of an indefensible security posture constitutes an actionable injury per se. By shifting the legal focus from the 'event' of the breach to the 'condition' of insecurity, this article proposes a normative realignment of tort law to address the 'silent' harms of compromised integrity, ensuring that invisible risks do not translate into unredressed societal externalities.

title: Agency Conflicts and Effort Misallocation in Brokerage Relationships
affiliations: Saint Mary's University, Canada - Department of Finance, Information Systems & Management Science

detail.title: Agency Conflicts and Effort Misallocation in Brokerage Relationships
detail.abstract: This paper investigates whether agents who have information advantage and serve multiple clients engage in prioritization that favors certain clients at the cost of others, amplifying agency conflicts. We study this question in the context of real estate brokerage, where one-stop sellers, who use the same agent to buy in close succession, create differential incentives that may induce effort misallocation. Our multi-client effort allocation model predicts that agents optimally tilt effort toward one-stop sellers, selling their house higher and faster while reducing payoffs for other impacted sellers. Using granular transaction data from Quebec's (Canadian province) housing market, we document that one-stop sellers sell their homes at a price premium compared to similar properties sold by other moving-sale sellers. However, the same agent sells houses slower and at a price discount for their impacted sellers than for one-stop sellers. In addition, this effort misallocation imposes negative externalities at the aggregate level: compared to non-impacted sellers, impacted sellers experience longer time-on-market and lower sale likelihood. We also show that agents strategically prioritize listings of their one-stop sellers, listing their houses timely on markets and increasing their likelihood of sales in each month. This paper documents a novel form of agent bias in which agents may favor certain sellers, leveraging information asymmetries to reallocate effort strategically. This behavior reflects underlying agency conflicts in delegated brokerage and highlights how incentive structures can generate systematic distortions in sellers' outcomes.

detail.abstract: Can an allocation algorithm be designed to not only distribute resources efficiently but also generate reliable economic statistics? As AI and high-frequency data reshape financial infrastructure, traditional "winner-takes-all" rules are failing-they generate noisy, unstable data that undermines auditability and policy monitoring. To solve this, we propose FIRM-L (Fair and Incentive-compatible Randomized Mechanism). Think of it as a mechanism with a "volume knob" (temperature control) that turns chaotic cliff-edge competition into a smooth, predictable curve. We mathematically prove that FIRM-L ensures fairness (via Lipschitz stability) and honesty (truthfulness-in-expectation) without sacrificing speed. Furthermore, we design an AI-driven controller that automatically tunes this mechanism in real-time, adapting to market shocks to protect welfare while keeping the market stable and auditable.

title: Relational Systems Theory: Drift Dynamics and Thresholds in Coupled Relational Ecologies

detail.title: Relational Systems Theory: Drift Dynamics and Thresholds in Coupled Relational Ecologies
detail.abstract: Relational Systems Theory (RST) extends Truth Stabilization Theory (TST) by shifting the unit of analysis from positions within a single relational system to an interacting ecology of systems (institutions, platforms, infrastructures, species, or other coupled subsystems). Each system i ∈ N carries its own representational misalignment di(t), structural-distance loading λi, epistemic capacity κi, and sphere of influence Si. RST introduces an explicit cross-system coupling matrix A, allowing misalignment generated in one system to propagate into others as imported distortion. This yields a minimal drift dynamic of the form di(t + 1) = (1+αλi −βκi) local multiplier Mi di(t) + γ AjiSjdj(t) + εi(t), j∈N and an ecological threshold criterion: when the spectral radius of the induced ecology update matrix exceeds unity, the coupled system-of-systems enters a drift-amplifying regime, even if many individual subsystems would be stable in isolation. We present a networked simulation demonstrating how a single highly influential and weakly stabilized subsystem can dominate total ecological drift D(t) = iSidi(t) and induce cascading misalignment across otherwise resilient nodes, and we illustrate how node-level interventions in λ and κ reduce (but need not eliminate) ecological drift under coupling.

detail.abstract:
This paper introduces the Sovereign Surplus Capacity Index (SSCI), a new macro-financial indicator designed to measure the sovereign's capacity to expand net financial assets without generating inflationary
  pressure, destabilizing credit dynamics, or relying on fragile external funding conditions. Modern economies operate through fiscal cycles as much as monetary cycles, yet we lack a unified, data-driven measure of
   non-inflationary fiscal space. The SSCI solves this gap by integrating seven macro pillars—safe fiscal deficit, labor-market resource expansion, productivity growth, inflation pressure, private credit cycle
  conditions, foreign-sector balance, and income-transmission strength—into a single composite index.

  The SSCI provides a systematic way to quantify the conditions under which sovereign deficit expansion translates into sustainable private-sector wealth rather than inflation, credit excess, or asset-price
  instability. The index is built entirely from publicly available data (Treasury MTS, BEA, BLS, FRED, BIS, TIC) and can be used for macro analysis, fiscal capacity assessment, and asset-allocation frameworks.

  Empirical validation using 65 years of U.S. data (1960–2024, 263 quarters) demonstrates that the SSCI successfully predicts major macro crises with exceptional advance warning and rigorous out-of-sample testing.
  The validation employs a gold-standard train-test split methodology: the SSCI framework was constructed using only 1960–2000 data (40 years), with all parameters, weights, and standardization procedures frozen.
  The resulting index was then applied to completely unseen data from 2001–2024 (24 years) to test predictive performance. This strict out-of-sample validation successfully predicted both the 2008 Financial Crisis
  (26.9 months early) and the 2022 Inflation Shock (23.8 months early), achieving a perfect 2-of-2 success rate on post-training crises with zero parameter adjustments.

  Extended historical testing against five major market crises spanning 1987–2022 shows the SSCI correctly predicted four of five events with lead times ranging from 16 to 27 months, including: (1) 1987 Black
  Monday (18.9 months early), (2) 1990–1991 Gulf War recession (16.3 months early), (3) 2008 Financial Crisis (26.9 months early), and (4) 2022 Inflation Shock (23.8 months early). The sole miss—the 2000–2002
  Dot-Com crash—occurred because SSCI remained elevated (112–138) during a period of strong fiscal fundamentals (budget surpluses, low inflation, high productivity), correctly identifying that the crisis stemmed
  from equity valuation excess rather than macroeconomic overheating. For macro/fiscal crises specifically, SSCI exhibits a perfect track record (4 of 4, 100%).

  The out-of-sample train-test split eliminates curve-fitting concerns and establishes high confidence in the framework's genuine predictive power. Additionally, the SSCI exhibits strong statistical relationships
  with inflation (R² = 14.3%, p < 0.001) and passes Granger causality tests at 2-4 quarter lags. These results establish the SSCI as one of the most rigorously validated public crisis prediction frameworks
  available.

title: What drives the spatiotemporal evolution of land use conflicts? Evidence of threshold effects from 19 Chinese urban agglomerations
affiliations: Institute of Mountain Hazards and Environment Chinese Academy of Sciences, affiliation not provided to SSRN, affiliation not provided to SSRN and affiliation not provided to SSRN

detail.title: What drives the spatiotemporal evolution of land use conflicts? Evidence of threshold effects from 19 Chinese urban agglomerations
detail.abstract: Land use conflicts (LUCs) have emerged as a critical constraint on regional sustainable development. However, existing research predominantly focuses on single-dimensional conflict identification, lacking systematic comparative analysis and composite assessment at the urban agglomeration scale. This study employs multi-source data from 19 Chinese urban agglomerations spanning 2000–2020 to construct a land use assessment framework that integrates structural and functional conflicts. Utilizing spatial Durbin models, machine learning, and generalized additive models, it systematically reveals the spatiotemporal evolution patterns and driving mechanisms of LUCs. The findings indicate: (1) LUCs exhibited a phased pattern of 'initial rise followed by decline,' with significant intensification occurring between 2000 and 2010, gradually easing post-2010 alongside ecological civilization strategies; (2) Spatial patterns demonstrate an 'east-high, west-low' divergence, with core eastern agglomerations such as Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei and the Yangtze River Delta Urban Agglomeration enduring persistent high conflict pressures, while northwestern regions experience lower conflict intensity; (3) The intensity of human footprint index (HFI) and terrain roughness index are dominant factors. Conflicts in eastern urban clusters primarily arise from high-intensity development pressures, whereas northwestern regions are constrained by topographical features. Key factors exhibit pronounced threshold effects: conflicts intensify sharply when HFI intensity and road network density exceed critical values. Vegetation cover demonstrates a non-monotonic influence, with the most acute contradictions between ecological conservation and development demands occurring in areas of moderate cover. This research provides scientific support for optimizing national spatial patterns, promoting coordinated regional development, and achieving dual carbon goals.

detail.abstract: This paper describes and analyzes a new survey methodology for reducing item non-response on financial measures. This "unfolding bracket" method is systematic and applicable in both face-to-face and telephone surveys. The proportion of missing observations for financial variables in national surveys is often in the 20-25% range and in some cases is as high as a third. With the unfolding bracket method the proportion of completely missing data can be cut by two-thirds. Furthermore, with appropriately chosen bracket breakpoints, the amount of the variance in the underlying measure recovered is quite high. We propose and demonstrate one method for choosing the breakpoints which employs the Downhill Simplex algorithm to maximize their explanatory value. Additionally, use of a Box-Cox transform of the actual data in conjunction with this algorithm, can result in breakpoints which are effective in explaining most of the underlying variance in both actual values and their log transforms. Since each of these metrics is appropriate for some uses this compromise is quite useful in meeting the needs of a wide variety of potential users. Finally, we investigate the effects of bracketing on the empirical validity of survey data. While we do find lower empirical validity for data from individuals exposed to brackets early in the survey instrument, this appears to be the result of self-selection rather than a direct effect of exposure to the methodology.

detail.title: The Impact of High-Speed Rail Station Development on Urban Form: Evidence from Beijing and Tianjin
detail.abstract:
The High-Speed Rail (HSR) was first constructed and operated in Japan in 1964. Today, several countries around Europe, Asia, and America have HSR services. As an emerging, high-speed ground transportation method, the HSR competes with and cooperates with road, air, and water transportation, and also contributes to economic development and passenger transportation. In 2008, China proposed a National High-Speed Rail Network Plan and began building the “JingHu Line,” which connects Beijing, Tianjin, and Shanghai.

This thesis focuses on the HSR construction in China, especially the construction of the “JingHu Line.” Beijing and Tianjin, the main cities served by this line, began reconstructing existing rail stations to meet the technical norms of HSRs. This thesis draws on existing literature about urban development, urban form, and high-speed rail stations to evaluate the impact of the HSR station on the surrounding area. It focuses especially on the reconstruction of high-speed rail stations in Beijing and Tianjin to examine the connections between HSRs and other urban transport methods, the emergence of new urban spaces, and land-use change in the station area.

In the thesis, I firstly review current literature and define three important terms, “high-speed rail,” “urban form,” and “rail station area,” which are the basis for this research. In the next section, I examine the evolving history of high-speed rail worldwide, which provides the background for this research and the main motivation for the construction of the Chinese High-Speed Network. Moreover, I review the features of HSR transportation, because the unique features of HSRs directly influence the changing form of surrounding areas. The “Urban Catalysts Theory” and “Linkage Theory” are introduced in Chapter 3 as the theoretical underpinning for this research. These two theories are tools to understand interactions between the HSR station and the surrounding area. Chapter three also reviews the current literature on the influence of HSR stations on a city. In the case study, I examine the construction of the HSR stations in Beijing and Tianjin to learn how the reconstruction projects were planned and built, how HSRs connect to the inner-city transportation network, and how the urban form changes in the station areas. Through this research, we can learn about the interactions between the construction of HSR stations and the development in the station area. Also, the review of reconstruction projects for HSR stations in Beijing and Tianjin provides experience for other cities that will have HSR services in the coming years.

title: Before Judgment, There Must be Structure: Fiscal Epistemology and the Conditions of Institutional Knowledge

detail.title: Before Judgment, There Must be Structure: Fiscal Epistemology and the Conditions of Institutional Knowledge
detail.abstract:
This paper examines the upstream conditions of institutional judgment: what qualifies as evidence, how information becomes decision-grade, and how judgment acquires institutional legitimacy. Its central claim is that judgment is not the starting point of institutional action. Judgment becomes possible only after heterogeneous materials are rendered into structured objects under admissible rules—objects that are traceable, reviewable, and bound to responsibility.

The paper advances Fiscal Epistemology as a theoretical frame for this domain, defining institutional knowledge through evidence discipline rather than narrative persuasion. It specifies how visibility, admissibility, and closure operate as preconditions of judgment, and why institutional coherence depends on maintaining this ordering. Fiscal Geometry (FG) is positioned as a praxis background—a representational craft for making institutional tension structurally readable—named but not developed as a method.

The contribution is intentionally upstream. Rather than predicting institutional collapse or engaging motive- or intent-based debates, the paper defines the conditions under which institutional judgment remains coherent, inspectable, and reviewable in information-dense environments. In this sense, it offers an interdisciplinary interface language: it distinguishes what narrative can explain from what institutions can process, and clarifies the threshold at which information becomes executable within accountable procedures.

detail.title: Dynamic Correlations vs. Orthogonal Factors: Hedging Effectiveness across Global Equities, Cryptocurrencies, and Commodities
detail.abstract: The financial regime spanning the post-pandemic recovery and the subsequent global monetary tightening cycle has rigorously tested the diversification properties of digital assets. While correlations between digital assets and global equities have intensified during this period of liquidity contraction, this study re-evaluates their strategic role within a trivariate portfolio anchored by commodities. We address the limitations of standard Gaussian frameworks by contrasting the Dynamic Conditional Correlation (DCC-GARCH) model against the Generalized Orthogonal GARCH (GO-GARCH) model to capture time-varying dependencies and structural risk drivers. To evaluate risk management efficacy, the study constructs Equal-Weighted, Maximum Diversification, and Minimum Variance Portfolios (MVP), with the optimization framework permitting short selling to explicitly manage volatility transmission. Empirical results demonstrate that the Maximum Diversification Portfolio fails to mitigate risk, yielding negative hedging effectiveness due to forced exposure to idiosyncratic volatility. Conversely, the Minimum Variance Portfolio delivers superior performance across all specifications. Crucially, the analysis identifies commodities as a vital volatility absorber, stabilizing the portfolio against the heightened correlation between equities and digital assets. These findings confirm that while digital asset risks have evolved, dynamic hedging strategies utilizing factor-based models and commodity integration can effectively enhance portfolio resilience during regime shifts.

detail.abstract: High-stakes institutional documents such as immigration notices, benefits letters, school compliance communications, and legal correspondence often fail non-expert readers not only through language barriers but through a "meaning-to-action" gap. Recipients may translate words yet still misunderstand obligations, deadlines, and risk. This paper presents an exploratory qualitative study examining practitioner trust boundaries and perceived failure modes in AI-assisted document interpretation. Ten participants, including legal, educational, and nonprofit support practitioners from the United States, Costa Rica, El Salvador, and Portugal, completed a baseline interview, five daily micro-checks over a five-day pilot use period, and an end-of-week interview while interacting with an AI-based document interpretation system. Using reflexive thematic analysis, recurring patterns were identified in which institutional documents obscure consequential risk, AI outputs are accepted as interpretive scaffolding, and legally, financially, or institutionally binding actions are consistently deferred to human judgment. These findings are synthesized into a governance-oriented design framework, Explain, Flag, Defer, which proposes uncertainty-aware risk surfacing, explicit non-advisory constraints, and audit-support features to support responsible deployment. Findings reflect practitioner perceptions in a personal capacity and should be interpreted as exploratory indicators of trust, risk perception, and workflow alignment rather than evidence of institutional adoption or end-user outcomes.

detail.title: CJEU: INGSTEEL II (CASE C-547/22): Compensation for Lost Opportunity -A Pivotal Judgment That Changes Little

declarations.funderStatement: This paper was supported by the Scientific Grant Agency Ministry of Education, Science, Research and Youth of the Slovak Republic and Slovak Academy of Sciences (VEGA) within the project 1/0710/23 “Damages in competition law and public procurement - limits and challenges to effective enforcement of the European Union law”.

detail.abstract: The judgment of the Court of Justice of the European Union in INGSTEEL II (case C-547/22) appears, at first glance, to mark a significant step in the development of damages remedies for breaches of EU public procurement law, by precluding national legislation or practice that categorically excludes compensation for harm resulting from the loss of an opportunity to obtain a public contract. This commentary argues, however, that the judgment is less transformative than it initially seems. Although the Court confirmed that loss of opportunity cannot be excluded as a matter of principle from the scope of Article 2(1)(c) of the Remedies Directive, it neither recognised loss of opportunity as an autonomous head of damage under EU law nor clarified its content, conditions, or quantification. The paper situates INGSTEEL II within the broader context of the Remedies Directive's minimal harmonisation, the Court's fragmented case law on damages (including Commission v Portugal, Strabag, Spijker, and the Fosen-Linjen saga), and the tension between EU-level effectiveness requirements and Member States' procedural autonomy. Particular attention is paid to the Slovak legal context underlying the reference, revealing that the judgment does not substantially alter Slovak law, which already allows-at least in theory-compensation for loss of opportunity within the concept of lost profit. The analysis demonstrates that INGSTEEL II employs a "doublenegative" approach: rather than defining compensable harm, the Court merely prohibits its absolute exclusion. As a result, key issuessuch as causation, evidentiary standards, and damages in the context of framework agreements-remain unresolved and are left to national law. The commentary concludes that judicial harmonisation through case law cannot provide a coherent or comprehensive system of compensation for unlawfully excluded tenderers and argues that meaningful clarification requires legislative reform of the Remedies Directive, potentially inspired by the structure of Directive 2014/104/EU on antitrust damages.

title: Public Debt Management and Tax Policy Interactions

detail.title: Public Debt Management and Tax Policy Interactions
detail.abstract:
This study examines the interactions between public debt management and tax policy, focusing on how coordinated strategies can enhance fiscal stability and mitigate financial risks. Employing a mixed-methods approach, the research integrates an extensive literature review, comparative case studies of selected economies, and quantitative analysis of key debt and tax indicators. The findings indicate that effective public debt management, including optimal debt structuring and strategic borrowing, significantly contributes to fiscal resilience. Moreover, alignment with tax policy through measures such as revenue mobilization, progressive taxation, and efficient tax administration amplifies these benefits by reducing the likelihood of fiscal stress and enhancing government capacity to meet debt obligations. 
The analysis also reveals that uncoordinated debt and tax policies may exacerbate budgetary vulnerabilities, particularly in developing economies with constrained fiscal space. Based on these insights, the study recommends that policymakers adopt integrated frameworks where debt issuance strategies are closely aligned with tax policy objectives, supported by transparent reporting and monitoring mechanisms. Such an approach can strengthen fiscal discipline, improve debt sustainability, and provide a stable foundation for long-term economic growth. The findings have practical implications for government agencies, financial regulators, and international development partners seeking to design policies that balance borrowing needs with sustainable revenue generation.

detail.title: Turning Crisis into Opportunity: an Essay on the Cultural Preconditions of Contemporary Crisis Mentality through a Conceptual Analysis of Weiji

publicationDetails.detailsText: Journal of the History of Ideas in East Asia, (2), 2012

detail.abstract: This study examines the cultural preconditions of a popular conception in contemporary societies characterized by the idea of turning crisis into opportunity. Building on Reinhart Koselleck’s thesis regarding the conceptual origins of modern crisis mentality in European cultures, this paper presents an analysis of the conceptual history of weiji 危機 (the Chinese word for “crisis”) in the Chinese cultural-historical context. The modern use of weiji originated in the late Qing reform movement, which saw the emergence of a discourse and widespread consciousness of Chinese nationalism. The proliferation of weiji-talk found in Chinese public press during the thirty-year period 1895-1925 was indicative of larger cultural transformations involving changes in the cultural conception of history. Within this context, the concept of weiji became drafted into ideologies of nationalism, republicanism, and Communism, the operation of which all depended on the new cultural mentality regarding the nature of historical change as linear and man-made. For this reason, the conceptual histories of “weiji” and “crisis” could be said to have converged during the 20th century on the basis of a deeper convergence of their underlying cultural conception of history. This convergence has provided an important cultural precondition for not only the pervasive idea of turning crisis into opportunity in contemporary societies but also the emergence and evolution of powerful ideologies including nationalism, communism, industrialism, capitalism, and scientism in modern China.

title: Institutional Analysis of Crossmatch-to-Transfusion Ratios at a Tertiary Hospital

detail.title: Institutional Analysis of Crossmatch-to-Transfusion Ratios at a Tertiary Hospital
detail.abstract: Background: Efficient blood utilization is increasingly essential in Korea due to increasing transfusion demand and a declining donor pool. The crossmatch-to-transfusion (C/T) ratio reflects ordering efficiency; however, long-term institutional-level analyses are rare. This study examined 10-year C/T ratio trends and blood utilization patterns at a major tertiary hospital.Methods: We retrospectively analyzed red blood cell usage at Asan Medical Center between 2015 and 2024. Annual data on transfused units, completed crossmatches, and canceled crossmatch requests were obtained from the institutional blood bank information system. The C/T ratio was calculated as crossmatched units divided by transfused units. Autologous transfusions, whole blood transfusions, and massive transfusion protocol activations were excluded. Trends were assessed by usage type (ward, surgery, outpatient, and emergency) and by department.Results: Annual transfused units ranged from 59,731 to 86,063, with institutional C/T ratios stable at 1.12–1.17. Surgical services exhibited the highest cumulative C/T ratio (1.55), whereas outpatient utilization exhibited the lowest (1.03). Ward and emergency services exhibited intermediate ratios (1.04 and 1.05, respectively), with gradual improvement over time. In 2024, most departments maintained efficient ratios of 1.02–1.10; higher ratios were observed in the Pediatric Surgery (1.52) and Vascular Surgery (1.33) departments.Conclusions: This decade-long study demonstrated efficient blood utilization with significant variation across clinical settings. These findings suggest that a single universal C/T ratio may be inappropriate; interpretation should consider specific operational context, particularly between surgical and nonsurgical services. These findings provide a foundation for multi-center studies to develop standardized transfusion efficiency metrics.

title: National Smart Fuel Network: An IT-Driven Logistics Framework to Reduce Fuel Waste and Strengthen Energy Security

detail.title: National Smart Fuel Network: An IT-Driven Logistics Framework to Reduce Fuel Waste and Strengthen Energy Security
detail.abstract: Fuel supply chains remain vulnerable to blind spots between production, storage, and distribution nodes, especially during disruptions when fragmented data slows response and increases waste. This paper proposes the National Smart Fuel Network (NSFN), an interoperable, IT-driven framework that integrates IoT telemetry (including satellite-enabled connectivity for remote corridors), warehouse and transportation system integration (WMS/TMS), and decision-support analytics to improve in-transit visibility, inventory accuracy, and disruption management. Using publicly available indicators combined with scenario-based modeling, NSFN performance is compared against a baseline fragmented network. Across normal, moderate-disruption, and severe-disruption scenarios, the model indicates potential reductions in fuel waste of 36-40%, improvements in inventory accuracy to 96-98%, reductions in delivery delays of 40-50%, and response-time improvements of 30-35%. The paper contributes (1) a reference architecture for end-to-end fuel logistics observability, (2) a reproducible evaluation approach with clear metrics and sensitivity checks, and (3) governance and security considerations for trusted data sharing across stakeholders.

title: Generational Differences in the Workplace: A Critical Review and Evidence-Based Framework for Organizational Practice

detail.title: Generational Differences in the Workplace: A Critical Review and Evidence-Based Framework for Organizational Practice
detail.abstract: The concept of generational differences has become deeply embedded in organizational discourse, shaping human resource practices, leadership development programs, and workplace policies. This article provides a comprehensive critical review of the empirical literature on generational differences in workplace values, attitudes, and behaviors. Synthesizing evidence from meta-analyses, longitudinal studies, and cross-cultural research, we find that the prevailing narrative of distinct generational cohorts with fundamentally different work orientations is largely unsupported by rigorous empirical evidence. Effect sizes for generational differences are consistently small, typically explaining less than 2% of variance in workplace outcomes, while within-generation heterogeneity substantially exceeds between-generation differences. We critically examine the "digital native" construct and its application to younger workers, finding limited empirical support for claims of inherent technological superiority. We further address the cultural specificity of Western generational frameworks and their limited applicability in non-Western contexts. The article proposes a contextual contingency framework that reconceptualizes age-related workplace dynamics through the integration of lifespan development theory, career stage models, sociohistorical context analysis, and intersectional perspectives. We provide specific attention to Generation Z's workforce entry amid unprecedented circumstances and examine implications for remote and hybrid work arrangements. Practical implications for evidence-based management are discussed, including recommendations for replacing generation-based interventions with approaches grounded in individual differences, life stage considerations, and organizational context. A detailed methodological agenda for future research addresses the age-period-cohort identification problem and proposes specific designs for advancing knowledge in this domain.

title: Increasing Resiliency of Critical Infrastructure Supply Chains: An IT-Driven Framework for Visibility, Buffering, and Rapid Recovery

detail.title: Increasing Resiliency of Critical Infrastructure Supply Chains: An IT-Driven Framework for Visibility, Buffering, and Rapid Recovery
detail.abstract: Critical-infrastructure supply chains that move food, medical supplies, fuel, and other essential goods are vulnerable to cascading failures when demand spikes, transportation capacity tightens, and information is fragmented across nodes. This paper proposes a practical resiliency framework that combines multi-node network design, adaptive inventory buffers, and a shared visibility and risk layer integrating WMS/TMS signals, IoT events, and early-warning indicators. The framework supports proactive disruption detection, coordinated allocation during shortages, and faster recovery through dynamic routing, pre-positioning, and cross-node replenishment policies. We present a reference architecture, an implementation blueprint for operators and public-private partners, and an evaluation approach using measurable outcomes such as service continuity, recovery time, stockout duration, and buffer efficiency. The proposed approach emphasizes interoperability, governance, and security so that heterogeneous actors can collaborate without centralizing sensitive commercial data. The result is a scalable blueprint for improving continuity of essential-goods distribution during natural hazards, labor constraints, cyber incidents, and other high-impact disruptions.

detail.abstract: Transitioning heavy-duty freight to low-carbon energy requires synchronized expansion of renewable electricity, green-hydrogen supply, and zero-emission vehicle (ZEV) fleets. This study introduces a stochastic multi-agent optimization framework to study market-based interaction outcomes of freight systems. The proposed framework links long-term infrastructure investments with short-term operational decisions for decentralized renewable generators, conventional plants, freight distributors, and mixed battery electric vehicles (BEV) and fuel cell electric vehicle (FCEV) fleets. A Texas case study illustrates system interactions across major freight corridors and highlights the roles of existing generator capacity, solar resources availability, and strategic investment of solar panels and electrolysis. Comparing the decentralized equilibrium with a centralized planner shows that the centralized planner invests substantially more in solar and hydrogen to reduce charging congestion and balance energy across hubs. Sensitivity analyses show that green hydrogen plays its largest role when conventional generation capacity is tight and renewable costs are low, whereas high conventional generation capacity shifts the system toward BEV charging. These interconnected findings highlight the importance of jointly considering resource availability, energy infrastructure, and freight technologies when designing targeted policies to steer decentralized markets toward long-term decarbonization goals.

detail.abstract:
• The rise of US dollar-linked stablecoins – digital tokens designed to maintain a constant one-for-one value with the US dollar – following the 2025 GENIUS Act poses potential risks to Canada’s monetary sovereignty and payment-system oversight. Without a clear domestic framework, Canadian payments could increasingly migrate to foreign-issued stablecoins and exchange platforms, weakening regulatory control and complicating monetary policy transmission.
  • Canada’s Stablecoin Act is a necessary first step but leaves critical design choices to the implementation phase. While the Act designates the Bank of Canada as the primary regulator and establishes baseline requirements for reserves and redemption, detailed rules on eligible assets, operational standards, insolvency treatment, and coordination with securities regulators remain unresolved.
  • This Commentary recommends a two-track regulatory model that aligns regulation with economic function rather than technology, giving Canada a viable path to shape its payments future rather than default to foreign stablecoin standards. Pure payment stablecoins should operate under Bank of Canada oversight as fully backed payment instruments, while tokenized bank deposits should remain within existing prudential banking regulatory frameworks. This approach promotes innovation while preserving financial stability and consumer protection.
  • Integrating stablecoins with a central bank digital currency (CBDC) could strengthen competition, resilience, and interoperability, and position Canada to compete effectively in the digital payments revolution. A CBDC, at minimum in wholesale form, would provide a neutral settlement layer, support orderly redemptions through central bank liquidity access, and enhance Canada’s ability to pursue international equivalency agreements while maintaining control over domestic payment infrastructure.

detail.abstract: The long-distance evacuation of electric vehicles (EVs) presents significant challenges for disaster management due to their limited driving range and constrained charging infrastructure. EVs with long charging times can create negative externalities for all other EVs waiting in queues, especially during evacuation scenarios. This study investigates the use of express charging lanes to reduce overall evacuation delays. We propose optimization models to optimize the allocation of charging plugs for express and regular charging, considering both user equilibrium and system optimal scenarios. To account for heterogeneities and uncertainties, such as stochastic EV arrival patterns and variable charging demands, we further develop numerical simulation models to quantify the delay distribution. We found that separating EVs with lower charging demand has the potential to minimize total system delay. The proposed models can identify the optimal level of express charging plug allocation to minimize the total charging delay without centralized enforcing traffic distribution. In addition, the model enables government agencies to estimate the required charging resources to fulfill timely evacuation within a given time window. The insights generated by the proposed theoretical models have been validated using agent-based simulation, where uncertainties can be flexibly represented.

title: Structural Market Behavior and Systematic Trading: Multi-Instrument Validation of the BLT Engine

detail.title: Structural Market Behavior and Systematic Trading: Multi-Instrument Validation of the BLT Engine
detail.abstract: This report presents a comprehensive empirical evaluation of the BLT Engine, a systematic trading engine assessed through multi-year, tick-level historical simulation and statistical robustness diagnostics. The primary objective of this document is not to disclose the internal mechanics or theoretical construction of the engine, but rather to analyze its observable behavior under real historical market conditions. Emphasis is placed on performance consistency, risk containment, equity stability, and sensitivity to trade-sequence variability. All results presented in this report are derived from deterministic historical back testing conducted over extended time horizons (spanning multiple market regimes), using high-fidelity tick data where available. The evaluation framework is uniform across tests, ensuring that observed differences in performance are attributable to market structure rather than execution artefacts. Key performance indicators include absolute profitability, drawdown characteristics, win rate stability, trade distribution properties, and risk-adjusted metrics such as profit factor and Sharpe ratio. These metrics are complemented by Monte Carlo stress testing, in which realized trades are randomly reordered to generate a large ensemble of alternative equity trajectories. The inclusion of Monte Carlo resampling allows for a rigorous assessment of robustness, helping to determine whether performance depends on favorable sequencing or instead reflects a persistent structural edge. Particular attention is given to the dispersion of outcomes, worst case equity paths, and the absence of account ruin across simulated scenarios. This report is intended for professional audiences, including quantitative traders, systematic strategy developers, and institutional evaluators, seeking a transparent, data-driven assessment of systematic trading performance without exposure of proprietary implementation details.

title: Inventory Planning under Demand and Yield Uncertainties: A Doubly Linear Decision Rule Approach
affiliations: , City University of Hong Kong, Department of Decisions, Operations and Technology, CUHK Business School, The Chinese University of Hong Kong, School of Business, Ningbo University and City University of Hong Kong (CityU)

detail.title: Inventory Planning under Demand and Yield Uncertainties: A Doubly Linear Decision Rule Approach
detail.abstract: Effectively planning multi-stage inventory requires careful consideration of both demand and yield uncertainties, as each significantly impacts decision quality. However, addressing these uncertainties jointly is challenging because they are influenced by unpredictable and sequentially revealed factors. In addition, the joint distribution of demand and yield is generally unknown in practice, and this distributional ambiguity further complicates the design of reliable policies. In this work, we propose a factor-based model to account for demand and yield uncertainties. To capture the distributional ambiguity, we formulate a distributionally robust multi-stage inventory planning problem. In our model, order quantities are determined sequentially and incorporate information from previous stages, resulting in an adaptive and robust policy. To address the computationally intractable bilinear constraints arising in the model's exact reformulation, we propose a novel doubly linear decision rule that captures both uncertainties and preserves tractability by reformulating the bilinear constraints for efficient and scalable optimization. Numerical experiments show that our model is able to make predictions for demand and yield at higher accuracy, and it achieves cost efficiency as well as robustness compared to benchmark strategies while maintaining computational tractability.

detail.abstract: Climate change is humanity’s greatest challenge for the XXIst century. Its effects will be felt for generations to come. In light of the enormity of the challenge, bank regulators are moving, yet reforms are neither homogeneous nor comprehensive. The EU is clearly more committed to the effort than any other player, and even within the EU, attitudes are cautious towards Pillar 1 (prudential requirements) and macroprudential measures, bolder towards Pillar 3 (market discipline through disclosures), and Pillar 2 (supervisory review), though more uneven on the latter. This does not follow a scientific logic (due to the high uncertainty of climate risk) but a policy logic, since legislators and regulators tend to follow a path of minimum resistance, and undertake first the reforms that require them a lower epistemic burden.

title: The Word "Run": A Proof of Concept for Premise Misalignment
affiliations: Independent Researcher

detail.title: The Word "Run": A Proof of Concept for Premise Misalignment
detail.abstract:
This paper challenges the widely cited claim that the English word “run” is the most complex word in the language, a conclusion typically drawn from its unusually large number of dictionary definitions. It argues that this conclusion rests on a category error: measuring conceptual complexity by counting surface-level outputs rather than identifying the underlying generative rule.

Using a structural analysis, the paper demonstrates that “run” operates as a single, minimal operator denoting the execution of a self-contained, continuous, forward-propelled process. The apparent multiplicity of meanings reflects the broad applicability of this operator across physical, mechanical, computational, social, and spatial domains—not semantic ambiguity.

This case serves as a proof of concept for premise misalignment, illustrating how expert narratives can mistake widespread invariance for complexity. The analysis suggests that similar misclassifications may underlie broader cognitive and institutional errors, where noise is mistaken for structure and description for explanation.

detail.abstract: This paper develops a dynamic insurance market model comprising two competing insurance companies and a continuum of insureds, and examines the interaction between strategic underreporting by the insureds and competitive pricing between the insurance companies under a Bonus-Malus System (BMS) framework. For the first time in an oligopolistic setting, we establish the existence and uniqueness of the insureds' optimal reporting barrier, as well as its continuous dependence on the BMS premiums. For the 2-class BMS case, we prove the existence of Nash equilibrium premium strategies and conduct an extensive sensitivity analysis on the impact of the model parameters on the equilibrium premiums.

detail.abstract: Asset pricing theory and risk management require accurate characterization of the complete distribution of returns, not just means, variances, and kurtosis. We document that standardized asset returns exhibit a universal symmetric wave-like deviation from normality appearing identically across equities, foreign exchange, cryptocurrencies, credit spreads, and VIX. This pattern persists for a century, remains invariant to temporal aggregation and portfolio diversification, and reflects a single dominant systematic factor. Ignoring this structure can lead to systematic underestimates of Value-at-Risk by 2.2-3.3 percentage points, translating to $2.2-3.4 billion errors per $100 billion portfolio. We show that consumption-based stochastic discount factors account for 61-79% of this distributional structure using conventional preference parameters. Independent approaches to constructing risk-neutral returns (both consumption and options-based) produce overlapping distributional shapes while markedly disagreeing on return levels. The equity premium puzzle therefore concerns levels and not the distributional shape of returns.

detail.title: The Anatomy of Decarbonizing Firms
detail.abstract: We study the firm-level drivers of corporate decarbonization using a global panel combining financial characteristics, balance-sheet indicators, ESG metrics, macroeconomic variables, and firms' greenhouse gas emissions. Emission trajectories exhibit strong persistence, with past emissions the dominant predictor of future performance. However, firms with larger carbon footprints also display greater abatement potential, creating opportunities for targeted stewardship and capital reallocation. We identify adoption of Science-Based Targets (SBT) as a significant catalyst for emission reductions and provide causal evidence that credible, externally validated climate commitments accelerate decarbonization. We develop machine-learning models that outperform heuristic benchmarks in forecasting one-year-ahead abatement, especially in hard-to-abate sectors, and we show that such forecasts can help further curtail portfolio-level emissions. Nevertheless, our results indicate that, given current emission trends in the cross-section of firms, building portfolios with net zero objectives for 2050 remains an open challenge.

publicationDetails.detailsText: The University of Auckland Business School Research Paper Series
